sources.notes: CRE workflows use Go or TypeScript SDKs, compile with CRE CLI, and run across a DON.
Deploying workflows to a Chainlink DON requires Early Access approval.
CRE supports private and onchain ethereum-mainnet workflow registries.
Execution capabilities including HTTP, Confidential HTTP, and EVM use built-in consensus.
Capability DON nodes execute independently and aggregate through BFT consensus.
HTTP client requests are node-level actions wrapped in consensus aggregation.
Confidential HTTP requests execute inside a secure enclave with secret templates and optional encrypted responses.
Deployed HTTP-triggered workflows require cryptographically signed requests from authorized EVM addresses.
CRE quotas are subject to change and include organization and workflow registry limits.
Functions sunset dates and migration guidance; use CRE rather than Functions for new work.

capabilities.name: HTTP Client
capabilities.consensus_behavior: Built-in consensus aggregation across capability DON nodes.
capabilities.router_use: Call deterministic or idempotent inference endpoints and aggregate structured outputs.
constraints: Inference endpoint should be deterministic by request hash and generation parameters.
POST endpoints must avoid duplicate side effects or use the documented single-execution/cache pattern.
Responses should be structured JSON for stable aggregation.

capabilities.name: Confidential HTTP Client
capabilities.consensus_behavior: Confidential request execution with CRE capability consensus around the workflow result.
capabilities.router_use: Send sensitive prompts or credentials through enclave-backed confidential requests.
constraints: Use vault-style secret templates for sensitive headers or body fields.
Treat evidence as confidential-compute/TEE evidence, not a ZKML proof by itself.
Plan encrypted response handling before sending sensitive prompt material.

capabilities.name: EVM Client
capabilities.consensus_behavior: CRE EVM capability operations participate in built-in consensus.
capabilities.router_use: Anchor verifier events or write receipt hashes to an app verifier contract.
constraints: Requires target chain configuration and consumer/verifier contract design.
Onchain writes introduce gas costs and irreversible public metadata.
Do not place raw prompts, PII, or secrets onchain.

capabilities.name: HTTP Trigger
capabilities.consensus_behavior: Starts deployed workflows after CRE validates signed trigger requests.
capabilities.router_use: Let the Python bridge submit canonical consensus requests on demand.
constraints: Production triggers require authorized EVM signing keys.
Requests need replay-safe IDs, nonces, and deadlines.
Live trigger tests must be opt-in.

quotas.router_design_implication: Prefer one configurable workflow with model/proof policy IDs instead of one workflow per model.

required_before_production: Confirm billing account or subscription mechanism.
Confirm paid usage limits and alerting.

recommended_first_path.capability: HTTP Client for non-sensitive deterministic endpoints; Confidential HTTP if prompts or credentials are sensitive
recommended_first_path.workflow_language: TypeScript or Go after team preference is confirmed
recommended_first_path.onchain_verifier_contract: defer unless production audit or smart-contract consumption requires it
